title: Fpqc descent of separatedness and the full valuative lifting property
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $q:E\to X$ be a morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering family of schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Put $E_i=E\times_XU_i$ and let $q_i:E_i\to U_i$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. A morphism $p:H\to T$ here is called separated if its diagonal $H\to H\times_TH$ is a closed immersion, meaning that every scheme base change of that diagonal is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Say that $p$ has the full valuative lifting property if for every valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], every $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$, and every $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to H$ over $b|_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, there is a unique $\widetilde a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to H$ over $b$ extending $a$. If each $q_i$ is separated and has this lifting property, then $q$ is separated and has the same lifting property. No quasi-compactness or finite-type assumption on $q$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9, p.67, descent of the valuative criterion in the forward inclusion; separatedness: Stacks spaces-descent.tex Tag 0421 (lemma-descending-property-separated); morphism descent: Tag 04P2 (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms). The valuation-extension argument expanding the descent assertion is recorded in the repair report.

proof.text: To prove separatedness, take any scheme $T$ and any map $T\to E\times_XE$, given by two maps $s,t:T\to E$ over the same map $T\to X$. Their equalizer $W=E\times_{E\times_XE}T$ is a scheme: it is also the pullback of the representable diagonal $E\to E\times E$ along $(s,t)$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The schemes $T_i=T\times_XU_i$ form an fpqc covering of $T$ by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. The map $W\times_TT_i\to T_i$ is the scheme test of the diagonal of $q_i$ given by the two induced maps to $E_i$; hence it is a closed immersion by the hypothesis on $q_i$. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to the scheme map $W\to T$. It is a closed immersion. This holds for every scheme test, exactly the required separatedness of $q$. All identifications here follow by describing a point as a pair of equal sections, so impose no representability on $E$ itself.

source.place: Tag 0421, lemma-descending-property-separated, diagonal argument; scheme-test reduction using descent.tex Tag 02L6

proof.text: Fix a valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $K$, a base map $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, and the given generic map $a$. There is at most one extension over $b$. Indeed, for any two extensions their equalizer is a closed immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}R$ by step 1. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] it has the form $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$. Equality on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ says that every element of $J$ maps to zero in $K$. Since $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, $J=0$, and the extensions are equal. This argument includes the case where $R$ is a field.

source.place: Separated diagonal gives uniqueness; direct affine equalizer calculation

proof.text: Pull the given cover back to $\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] the schemes $V_i=U_i\times_X\operatorname{Spec}R$ are an fpqc covering. Thus every projection is flat and some $V_i$ has a point above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Apply [lem-a1-flat-valuation-lifting] to this projection and the identity map of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Obtain an injective local map $R\to R\prime$ of valuation rings and a map $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to V_i$. Write $K\prime=\operatorname{Frac}(R\prime)$; injectivity induces $K\hookrightarrow K\prime$. The composite to $U_i$ is compatible with the specified map to $X$.

The $R$-modules $R\prime$ and $K\prime$ are torsion-free because they embed into the field $K\prime$ and $R\to K\prime$ is injective. Both are therefore flat by [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat]. The local map $R\to R\prime$ is faithfully flat, with surjective spectrum map, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. The affine morphism is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Consequently $v:\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an fpqc covering: it is flat and surjective. Every affine open $V$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so finitely many principal opens $D(r_j)$ contained in $V$ cover $V$. Their inverse images $D(\iota(r_j))$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime$ are affine, and their images are exactly $D(r_j)$ by surjectivity. They supply the finite family required in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Also $K\to K\prime$ is a flat local map of fields by the same torsion-free criterion and hence faithfully flat by the same local-map lemma; its spectrum map is an fpqc covering as well.

source.place: Tag 0539, lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat; algebra.tex Tag 00HR, lemma-local-flat-ff; topologies.tex Tag 03L7, affine case

proof.text: The map to $V_i$ gives a base map $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to U_i$. Together with $a|_{\operatorname{Spec}K\prime}$ it gives a generic map $\operatorname{Spec}K\prime\to E_i$. Apply the assumed full lifting property of $q_i$ to this valuation diagram. Compose the resulting lift with $E_i\to E$ to obtain $e\prime:\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to E$ over $X$, whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K\prime$ is the base change of $a$. This applies to the actual chosen index $i$; no trivialization of $E$ or finite-type property is needed.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9, p.67, descent assertion: apply the local lifting hypothesis

proof.text: Put $B=R\prime\otimes_RR\prime$ and $D=K\prime\otimes_RK\prime=K\prime\otimes_KK\prime$. These spectra are the indicated fibre products: the tensor algebra universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and the contravariant affine-spectrum equivalence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] give the same pairs of compatible ring maps. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] twice to $R\prime\hookrightarrow K\prime$, first tensoring with the $R$-flat module $R\prime$, then with the $R$-flat module $K\prime$ from step 4 (interchanging tensor factors when needed). It follows that $B\to D$ is injective. The last displayed equality holds since every nonzero element of $R$ is already invertible in both $K\prime$ factors. On $\operatorname{Spec}D$ the two pullbacks of $e\prime$ are both the pullback of $a$ along the common map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Their equalizer on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is closed by step 1, hence is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its pullback to $D$ is the whole spectrum, so $JD=0$. Injectivity of $B\to D$ forces $J=0$. Therefore the two maps agree on the entire overlap $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R\prime$.

source.place: Tag 04P2, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms, compatibility required for descent; explicit affine overlap verification

proof.text: Use [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] with base scheme $X$, target $E$, domain $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and the singleton fpqc cover $v$ of step 4. Step 6 is exactly its compatibility condition. It gives an $X$-morphism $\widetilde a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to E$ pulling back to $e\prime$. Its restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $a$ agree after the fpqc field extension $\operatorname{Spec}K\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, since $e\prime|_{K\prime}=a|_{K\prime}$. The equality clause of the same sheaf lemma, again over $X$, gives $\widetilde a|_K=a$. This is the required lift; uniqueness was proved in step 2. The proof has used no quasi-compactness or finite-type assumption on $q$.

The item statement is unchanged, true, not weakened, and is what step 6 of lem-a1-proetale-local-system-representability uses. Step 1: the scheme equalizer W of two maps into E is tested on the base-changed fpqc cover T_i and descended with 02L6 applied to the scheme map W→T. Step 2: an ideal killed in the fraction field is zero. Steps 3–4: 089F applied with b=id gives an injective local map R→R'; torsion-free implies flat for R' and K', flat plus local gives faithfully flat, and the finite principal-open clause of the fpqc definition is checked explicitly. Step 6: R'⊗R'→K'⊗K' is injective by two flat-tensor applications; the two K-structures on D agree because nonzero r in R is invertible; the closed equalizer then forces J=0. Step 7: the 04P2 gluing, then the 04P2 uniqueness on {Spec K'→Spec K} recovers a. New nodes: lem-a1-flat-valuation-lifting matches 089F specialized to schemes, and lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf matches the 04P2 equalizer with scheme domains. Both are statement-only, record all three search kinds, have correct blueprint.from/via and are not clauses of the item. Duplicate check: lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent (023Q) has scheme targets only, and the other algebraic-space/fpqc nodes, the Nagata domination nodes and the proper specialization lift state different things. Accepted tool use: lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion (sk-thm-picard-rr) as generic closed-immersion descent. Batch-5 check: def-trf-algebraic-space and def-trf-valuation-ring are general definitions, and lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection and lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat are generic Mathlib algebra leaves. None of the four is part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, so all are accepted. Edge cases: X or E empty, R a field, the identity cover, and an infinite disjoint union (shows that properness must not be assumed). No SGA cited. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem closedDiagonal_and_fullValuativeLifting_of_fpqc_cover {X : Scheme.{u}} (E : AlgebraicSpace X) {I : Type u} (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X) (hcover : Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage X) (hlocal : ∀ i : I, IsSeparatedPresheafMap (terminal.from ((Over.map (f i)).op ⋙ E.obj.obj)) ∧ HasFullValuativeLifting ((Over.map (f i)).op ⋙ E.obj.obj)) : IsSeparatedPresheafMap (terminal.from E.obj.obj) ∧ HasFullValuativeLifting E.obj.obj
lean.note: Separatedness (closed diagonal, every scheme test a closed immersion) is the project's landed AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicSpace.IsSeparatedPresheafMap (Sheaf.TraceFormula.SpaceQCSeparatedEtaleLocal, the separatedness predicate of lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local) applied to the structure map terminal.from F; the terminal presheaf on Over X is h_X, so this is q : E -> X, and its presheaf pullback over the terminal object is E x_X E. The reviewer's fix replaced the delivered duplicate HasClosedDiagonal by it (H4). HasFullValuativeLifting is a real Prop definition spelling out the full valuative lifting property defined explicitly in this node; no project or Mathlib declaration states it for presheaves/algebraic spaces. For E over X, q is its structure morphism; precomposition with (Over.map (f i)).op is the functor of points of the actual base change E x_X U_i over U_i. No presentation, additional structure, finiteness hypothesis, or arbitrary comparison map is assumed.
